metaTitle: Export Enquiries: How Indian Manufacturers Get and Reply
metaDescription: What an export enquiry is, how to check if it is genuine, what to send in the first reply, and the website facts overseas buyers need before they enquire.
title: Export enquiries for Indian manufacturers: how to get them and how to reply
excerpt: A buyer three time zones away cannot visit your factory. Everything they need in order to risk an enquiry has to exist on your website.
intro: An export enquiry is a message from a buyer in another country asking about your product, price, minimum order, lead time or terms. For an Indian manufacturer it is the first step of an export sale, but it is only an opportunity once you have checked who is asking, what they need and whether you can supply it, and replied clearly and fast.

Selling to a buyer in the next state is mostly relationships and references. Selling to one who cannot visit the factory is a different problem: every reason to trust you has to be visible before they contact you, and the first reply decides whether the conversation continues. This guide covers both: how to qualify and answer an export enquiry, and what your website must show so the right buyers enquire in the first place.

sections.heading: How to check and answer an export enquiry
paragraphs: Treat every export enquiry as unqualified until you know four things: who the buyer is, what exactly they want, how much and when, and how they intend to pay and ship. Official export-promotion bodies give the same advice: reply promptly, completely and clearly, and ask the buyer about their business before you commit to terms ([export.gov](https://legacy.export.gov/article?id=Responding-to-Enquiries), [Austrade](https://export.business.gov.au/find-buyers-and-sales-partners/respond-to-sales-enquiries)).

Some enquiries are not genuine. Common warning signs are a free email address with no company website, a request for samples or documents to be sent before any specification is discussed, pressure to pay a registration or certification fee to the buyer's side, or payment terms that move all the risk to you. None of these proves fraud on its own, so verify before you spend money or share pricing files.

What to look for
What to ask or do
rows: Company name, website, address and a business email domain that match
Ask for the company profile; look up the website and any public company register for that country

Order size, one-off or recurring, target delivery date

list: Acknowledge within one working day, even if the full quotation takes longer, and say when it will arrive
Restate the requirement in your own words so both sides agree on the specification
Quote with currency, Incoterm, validity period, minimum order and lead time
Ask the qualifying questions from the table in the same reply
Attach a short company profile and link to the product and certification pages on your website
Log the enquiry with its source and next follow-up date, so it is not forgotten during a long export cycle

sections.heading: The buyer's actual question
paragraphs: An overseas or out-of-state buyer evaluating an unfamiliar Indian supplier is not primarily asking whether your product is good. They are asking whether engaging with you is a risk worth taking.

Underneath that: will this company still exist in eighteen months, can it hold the specification consistently across a production run, will it communicate when something goes wrong, and is it big enough to matter to but not so big that my order is insignificant.
Almost nothing on a typical manufacturer website addresses any of these. The site describes products. The buyer is assessing the company.

sections.heading: Certifications as pages, not PDFs
paragraphs: Certifications are the fastest trust signal available, and most manufacturers bury them in a downloadable PDF or a row of logos with no detail.

Give each meaningful certification a page: what it covers, the certifying body, the scope, and the validity period. This is findable in search, readable on a phone, and verifiable by a buyer doing diligence — none of which is true of a logo.

It also matters increasingly for AI answer surfaces, which a growing number of technical buyers consult before shortlisting. Content inside a PDF is substantially less likely to be read and cited than the same content as a page.

sections.heading: Named installations, where you are permitted
paragraphs: One named customer does more for an unfamiliar buyer than any number of claims about quality.

Many manufacturers cannot name customers, and that constraint is real. The workable middle is a described installation without the name: the sector, the scale, the specification, the year, the challenge. "A dairy processing facility in Maharashtra, 12 tonne capacity, commissioned 2024" is credible in a way "trusted by leading brands" is not.
Never publish a customer name without written permission. For a business selling on reliability, being caught overclaiming a relationship is not recoverable.

sections.heading: State capacity as a number
paragraphs: A buyer placing a significant order needs to know you can fulfil it, and "large manufacturing facility" tells them nothing.

Publish the numbers: plant area, monthly or annual production capacity in units, number of production lines, workforce size, and current lead times. These are the figures that let a buyer decide whether to enquire at all.
Lead time is the one most often omitted and most often asked. Publishing it filters out buyers whose timeline you cannot meet, which saves both sides a conversation.

sections.heading: Structure products by specification, not by marketing name
paragraphs: Internal product names mean nothing to someone who has not bought from you. Buyers search by what the thing does and by the numbers that define it.

Organise around the specification — capacity range, material, temperature range, power rating, standard complied with — and let the product name follow. Then each specification range becomes a page a buyer can actually find.

This is also how export enquiries arrive through search rather than through directories. A buyer searching for a specific capacity in a specific material finds a page about exactly that, or they find a competitor's.

sections.heading: Commit to a response time, and meet it
paragraphs: For an overseas buyer, the first reply is the entire basis for judging whether you will communicate well over a six-month project.
State the commitment on the page — one working day is a reasonable and achievable promise — and then meet it. A published commitment you miss is worse than none at all.

Time zones matter here. A buyer in Europe or North America sending an enquiry at the end of their day should not wait two of your working days for an acknowledgement. Even a holding reply that names when a technical answer will arrive is enough to keep the conversation alive.

sections.heading: Make the enquiry form export-aware
paragraphs: A domestic enquiry form asks for city and phone. An export buyer needs to tell you different things, and a form that cannot accept them signals you do not do this often.
list: Required specification or the standard to be complied with
Approximate order quantity and whether it is one-off or recurring
Whether they need documentation support for import
An international phone field that actually accepts their number

sections.heading: The systems behind the enquiry
paragraphs: Export cycles are long, multi-contact and easy to lose to silence. An enquiry in March may be an order in October, across a dozen emails, two sample shipments and a video call.

Nobody holds that in their head across several live opportunities, which is why the deals that go quiet are usually the ones that were forgotten rather than lost to a competitor. The mechanics are in [lead generation for industrial and deep-tech B2B](/blog/industrial-b2b-lead-generation-india).

In our [refrigeration and deep-technology partnership](/case-studies/deep-tech-b2b-expansion), the work was exactly this: positioning the technical capability so a commercial buyer could evaluate it, then putting B2B lead generation and business-development tracking behind it so long cycles were tracked rather than remembered.

sections.heading: What should an exporter ask an SEO agency?
paragraphs: Ask how the work will distinguish target buyer countries, product requirements and supported configurations. An export lead-generation agency should explain how enquiries enter your sales process and how the team will assess product fit; an overseas visitor is not automatically an export opportunity.

Agree the content review owner and the measurement window. Keep any unsupported certification, delivery promise or export claim out of the page. Connect the [industrial lead-generation framework](/blog/industrial-b2b-lead-generation-india) to your existing qualification process before deciding whether more content is needed.

takeaway: Publish certifications as pages, describe real installations even if you cannot name the customer, state capacity and lead time as numbers, organise products by specification, and commit to a response time you actually meet. A buyer who cannot visit your factory needs all of it before they will risk an enquiry.

faq.a: An export enquiry is a request from a buyer outside India for information on your product, such as price, specification, minimum order quantity, lead time or delivery terms. It becomes an export opportunity only after you confirm the buyer is genuine and that you can supply what they need on terms you accept.

faq.q: How do I know if an export enquiry is genuine?
faq.a: Check that the company name, website, address and email domain match, and that the buyer asks about a specific product or specification. Be careful with free email addresses, requests for samples or documents before any specification is discussed, and any request that you pay a fee to the buyer's side. Verify before you share pricing or spend money.

faq.q: How fast should I reply to an export enquiry?
faq.a: Acknowledge it within one working day and say when the full quotation will follow. Buyers in other time zones judge how you will communicate during the order by the speed and clarity of the first reply.

faq.q: What should a reply to an export enquiry include?
faq.a: Restate the requirement, then give the price with currency, the Incoterm, quotation validity, minimum order, lead time and payment terms. Ask the questions you still need answered, and link to the product and certification pages on your website.

faq.q: How can a manufacturer get more export enquiries from its website?
faq.a: Publish the facts an overseas buyer checks before enquiring: certifications as pages, capacity and lead time as numbers, products organised by specification, real installations, and an enquiry form that accepts country, port, specification and quantity. Those pages are also what search engines and AI answers can find and cite.
